_about: The 1519 tributary provinces of the Triple Alliance, for the clip Sheppard_Tlaxcalans_thought_they_used_Cortes (Dwarkesh map style; builder P, Oct 4 2026). Read by scripts/build-tlax-provinces.mjs -> generated/components/tlaxProvinces.ts. lon/lat WGS84. Province names in Codex Mendoza spelling (Berdan & Anawalt 1992); never drawn on screen.
source: Provincias tributarias de la Triple Alianza (s. XVI).svg, Wikimedia Commons, Yavidaxiu 2008 (CC BY-SA 3.0), after Solanes Carraro & Vela Ramírez, Atlas del México prehispánico, Arqueología Mexicana ed. especial 5 (2000): the 38 tributary provinces (Codex Mendoza; Barlow 1949) as green borders inside the red empire outline, the provincial head towns as red dots, the independent señoríos as black squares. The same author and atlas as the empire outline already in scripts/cortes-geo.json.
method: Parsed the SVG (green province lines, red outline, empire fill, coast, head-town circles). Georeferenced by a least-squares affine fit (lon, lat = affine(svg x, y)) to 33 towns with gazetteer lon/lat (head towns, the independent señoríos, the three alliance capitals; Tlapacoyan dropped, the map places it 68 km off the modern town) refined by coastline ICP against Natural Earth 10m (10 iterations, control points weight 3, p80 outlier cut): control rms 12.9 km (max 25 km, Tepeaca), coast median 5.0 km, p80 13 km. Each province = the flood fill of the line network from its head-town dot (the outline and outside-the-empire as barriers, line ends snapped to the nearest line within 3 map units). Unlabelled pixels (the lines themselves, and the parts of the cortes-geo.json empire outside this map's outline) take the nearest province label (8-neighbour dilation). Sampled onto a world raster (5 cells / world px) through the shared LCC; islands < 300 cells dropped; Citlaltepec's strip down the middle of the map's lake (the lake divided between the Tenochca and the Acolhua) left slivers on our larger 1519 lake's shores, so south of 19.56 N it goes to the nearest other province. Vectorised topologically: pixel-edge arcs between junctions, Gaussian-smoothed (sigma 0.52 world px, ends fixed) and simplified (0.044 world px), so neighbouring cells share identical edges; build-tlax-provinces.mjs clips each cell to EMPIRE_POLYS (the empire every cut draws). Oztoman merged into Tepecoacuilco (no line between them on the map); Petlacalco's pocket + the unassigned land round Tenochtitlan and Tlacopan = the Tenochca core.

georef.model: lon = c0 + c1*x + c2*y ; lat = d0 + d1*x + d2*y ; x,y = SVG viewBox units of Provincias_tributarias_de_la_Triple_Alianza_(s._XVI).svg

provinces.name: Tlatlauhquitepec
provinces.joined: Aug 1519: the Totonacs of Cempoala (a province of ~50 towns, ~50,000 warriors by Cortes's count) 'wished to become vassals ... and my friends'; 400 Cempoalans fought with him at Tlaxcala and Cholula. No siege contingent found. PROXY: Cempoala is not a Codex Mendoza province (a strategic province in Berdan et al. 1996, pp.286-87); it sits on the coast at the seam of this map's Tlatlauhquitepec and Cuauhtochco provinces, and this cell holds most of Totonacapan (Quiahuiztlan, Xalapa, Misantla).
provinces.source: Cortes, Second Letter (MacNutt 1908 vol. 1) pp.187, 202, 217; Berdan et al., Aztec Imperial Strategies (1996) pp.286-87.

provinces.name: Tepeacac
provinces.joined: Aug-Sep 1520 (Tepeaca submitted after a ~20-day campaign; its lords 'offered themselves as vassals'); Oct 1520 Huaquechula (voluntary: invited Cortes to expel the Mexica garrison; its warriors joined Sandoval at Chalco, Mar 1521); Oct-Nov 1520 Izucar (taken, then 'our friends and allies').
provinces.source: Cortes, Second Letter (MacNutt 1908 vol. 1) pp.305-07, 309, 315-17; Third Letter (vol. 2) pp.6, 37, 133; Ixtlilxochitl, Relacion decimotercera (Obras, ed. Chavero 1891) p.363.

provinces.name: Huaxtepec
provinces.joined: Mar-Apr 1521: Huaxtepec submitted to Sandoval ('in peace, though well chastised', with Yecapixtla) and hosted Cortes's force peacefully in April; Yautepec asked pardon. No siege contingent documented.

provinces.name: Chalco
provinces.joined: Jan 1521: the Chalca came over once Sandoval beat the Mexica force there; the lord's sons came to Texcoco; Tlalmanalco garrisoned as a frontier fort; Chalca fought at the siege (10,000 at the first entry, Ixtlilxochitl).
provinces.source: Cortes, Third Letter (MacNutt 1908 vol. 2) pp.22-24, 42, 61-62, 81; Ixtlilxochitl, Historia de la nacion chichimeca ch. XCV p.294.

provinces.name: Tepequacuilco
provinces.note: The map draws no line between Tepecoacuilco and the Oztoman garrison (Oztuma): one cell.

provinces.name: Cuauhnahuac
provinces.joined: Apr 1521: the lord submitted after the town was stormed; ~2 Jul 1521 they asked Cortes for help against Malinalco and Cuisco, and fought beside Andres de Tapia's 80 foot and 10 horse.
provinces.source: Cortes, Third Letter (MacNutt 1908 vol. 2) pp.48, 100-01; Ixtlilxochitl, Relacion decimotercera p.370.

provinces.name: Acolhuacan
provinces.joined: Jan-Feb 1521: Coatlinchan, Huexotla, Atenco, then Otumba; Don Fernando (Ixtlilxochitl's faction) installed at Texcoco; Acolman friendly by Mar 1521; Ixtlilxochitl's levy (30,000 + 20,000) arrived mid-June 1521. The ruler Coanacochtzin stayed with the Mexica.
provinces.source: Cortes, Third Letter (MacNutt 1908 vol. 2) pp.16, 20, 24-25, 36, 77-78; Ixtlilxochitl, Relacion decimotercera p.361.
provinces.note: The Acolhua domain: holds Texcoco (an alliance member, no province of its own on the map).

provinces.name: Malinalco
provinces.joined: ~late Jul 1521: with the Matlatzinca, the lords of Malinalco came to the camp, asked pardon and offered to serve (after Tapia's and Sandoval's raids).

provinces.name: Tollocan
provinces.joined: ~late Jul 1521: after Sandoval's raid the lords of Matalcingo (the Matlatzinca of the Toluca valley) came to the camp, asked pardon and offered to serve; they then sent warriors and food (Ixtlilxochitl).
provinces.source: Cortes, Third Letter (MacNutt 1908 vol. 2) p.106; Ixtlilxochitl, Relacion decimotercera pp.370-71; Diaz del Castillo ch. CLV (Lockhart 1844).

provinces.name: the Tenochca-Tepanec core (Tlacopan, Azcapotzalco, Tenayuca)
provinces.note: The map leaves the land round Tenochtitlan and Tlacopan unassigned (and squeezes Petlacalco into a pocket beside Tlacopan); north of 19.40 N it is the Tepanec / Tenochca core round the west shore: Tlacopan, Azcapotzalco, Tenayuca, found deserted / hostile in Feb 1521 (Cortes, Third Letter, MacNutt 1908 vol. 2 pp.33-34). Never flips.

provinces.name: Petlacalco (the southern lake towns)
provinces.joined: June 1521: Xochimilco came over mid-June (with the Otomi), then Iztapalapa, Huitzilopochco, Culhuacan, Mixquic and Cuitlahuac, before the 30 June defeat: they supplied canoes, warriors, food and huts for the camp. Diaz adds Coyoacan and 'all the other towns' on the fresh-water lake.
provinces.source: Cortes, Third Letter (MacNutt 1908 vol. 2) pp.73, 78-79, 84-86; Diaz del Castillo ch. CLI (Lockhart 1844).
provinces.note: Codex Mendoza ff.20r-v (Berdan & Anawalt 1992): Petlacalco collected from the southern basin - Huitzilopochco, Colhuacan, Cuitlahuac, Mixquic, Xochimilco (through its ward Olac); Hodge, Aztec City-States (1984) pp.94, 147-48. The cell = the unassigned land of the source map round the lake south of 19.40 N (a proxy line: the map draws no border here).

polities.name: Tlaxcala
polities.ref: Cortes, Third Letter (MacNutt 1908 vol. 2) p.60: 'more than fifty thousand' Tlaxcalan warriors arrived at Texcoco for the siege (25,000+ with Alvarado, 20,000+ with Olid, p.61). Diaz: 8,000 each to Alvarado and Olid (ch. CL).

polities.name: Huexotzinco
polities.ref: Ixtlilxochitl, Historia de la nacion chichimeca ch. XCIV p.287: more than 10,000; Cortes, Third Letter p.62: Huexotzinco, Cholula and Chalco together 'more than thirty thousand'.

polities.name: Cholula
polities.ref: Ixtlilxochitl, Historia de la nacion chichimeca ch. XCIV p.287: almost 10,000; Cortes, Third Letter p.62 (with Huexotzinco and Chalco, 30,000+).

polities.name: Teotitlan
polities.ref: Independent of the empire (source map) and hostile to it, so it turns orange in cut C; but no alliance with Cortes or contingent at the siege was found: weight 0 (CHANGED 2026-10-04, Fable's review).

polities.name: Tepeaca (with Huaquechula, Izucar)
polities.ref: Allied after Aug-Nov 1520 (see the cell's source); Huaquechula's warriors joined Sandoval at Chalco (Cortes, Third Letter p.37); no siege figure.

polities.name: Huaxtepec
polities.ref: Submitted Mar-Apr 1521 (Cortes, Third Letter pp.37-39, 45-46); no contingent documented.

polities.name: Chalco
polities.ref: Ixtlilxochitl, Historia de la nacion chichimeca ch. XCV p.294: 10,000 Chalca at the first entry into the city; Cortes, Third Letter p.62 (with Huexotzinco and Cholula, 30,000+).

polities.name: the Acolhua (Texcoco)
polities.ref: Cortes, Third Letter (MacNutt 1908 vol. 2) p.78: Ixtlilxochitl brought 'more than thirty thousand' to Cortes's camp and 20,000 to the other two camps (mid-June 1521); Ixtlilxochitl, Relacion decimotercera p.361: 50,000 (30,000 / 10,000 / 10,000).

polities.name: the Totonacs (Cempoala)
polities.ref: Allied Aug 1519 (Cortes, Second Letter pp.187, 202, 217: 400 Cempoalans at Tlaxcala and Cholula); no siege contingent found.

polities.name: Cuauhnahuac
polities.ref: Submitted Apr 1521; fought beside Tapia against Malinalco ~2 Jul 1521 (Cortes, Third Letter pp.48, 100-01; Ixtlilxochitl's ~40,000 for that joint force, Relacion decimotercera p.370, is not a siege figure).

polities.name: the Matlatzinca (Toluca)
polities.ref: Submitted ~late Jul 1521 and sent warriors and food (Cortes, Third Letter p.106; Ixtlilxochitl, Relacion decimotercera pp.370-71); no figure.

polities.name: Malinalco
polities.ref: Submitted ~late Jul 1521, offered to serve (Cortes, Third Letter p.106); no figure.

polities.name: the southern lake towns (Petlacalco)
polities.ref: Came over in June 1521 with canoes, warriors and food (Cortes, Third Letter pp.78-79, 84-86); no separate figure (Cortes counted 'more than a hundred thousand men, our friends' in camp one day, p.86).

total.ref: Ixtlilxochitl, Relacion decimotercera (Obras, ed. Chavero 1891) p.379: 'doscientos mil que fueron de la parte de los Espanoles'; Wikipedia 'Fall of Tenochtitlan' infobox 50,000-200,000 (citing Hassig 1994, page not checked). Spaniards: 86 horse, 118 crossbowmen and arquebusiers, 'seven hundred and odd' foot = ~904 at the 28 Apr 1521 muster (Cortes, Third Letter, MacNutt 1908 vol. 2 p.59).

contingents.rule: weight = documented warriors / 200,000 where a figure exists; the remainder (200,000 - the documented sum) is shared among the undocumented allied provinces in proportion to their area (km2). The three outer enclaves (Teotitlan, Metztitlan, Yopitzinco) have men 0: no contingent documented (CHANGED 2026-10-04).
